body: As mentioned previously, I favor putting the trivial branch in blocks while the nontrivial branch stays in-line - even if it results in more LOC :)
I fail to see how this one would be more trivial though (you can close this, of course :) )

You're right; in this case it's not as clear as in others.

Maybe this helps:
In the case of a loop, `continue` is usually more trivial than `return`, since `return` is a goal and `continue` means the current element is not what we are looking for.
It's more consistent to write code that has `continue` on the indented block and 'the other' code in non indented blocks. But I can see why you would disagree in this case :)

I would also use `if (override_prop) { return override_prop->get().variant; }`, `return`/`break`/`continue` are pretty much same complexity, so it's not adding any readability here. But won't insist on this change.
I don't have a super strong opinion on this one, so I'll accommodate and use the shorter positive variant as suggested :)
